questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill or downgrade is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a steep hill or downgrade ahead. The hill may be long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions right ahead. This sign warns you about a curve to the right.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Other drivers may not see you.
Cars behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect the light back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Increase your distance behind large vehicles to:

options.text: See around the sides of the vehicle.
Stop other drivers from passing the large vehicle.
Avoid getting caught in the vehicle's air flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: See around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead. Increase your distance behind trucks, buses, and trailers so you can see around them and see what is ahead on the road.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to help them return safely to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help them return safely to your lane.
questions.explanation: Allow the passing vehicle to return to your lane easily and safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your interstate speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you take the recommended dose.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You are responsible for knowing how your medicines affect your ability to drive.

questions.question: Help cars merge onto the freeway by:

options.text: Keeping your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If possible, move to another lane to create space. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed so they can enter traffic safely.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may cross it to pass when the way ahead is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a two-way road.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see traffic coming from both directions.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never pass or change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Also watch for other drivers trying to enter the same lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles display an orange and red triangle on the back. These include farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road direction is changing or the road is getting narrower. You will see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an approaching car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then continue looking ahead to track the position of the other vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to places where animals, people, and vehicles may cross the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends soon. Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the number of lanes is decreasing. Traffic must merge to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when it is dark. Use your headlights correctly and follow the rules for high and low beams. Never look directly at oncoming headlights as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes at any other time, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers entering the same lane.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You can pass on the right when it is safe.
You can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left. Make sure no traffic is coming toward you first. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels go off the edge of the road. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to steer back onto the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Slow down first, then check for traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Turning the wheel too hard can cause you to lose control or hit other cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire suddenly goes flat, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light braking.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change as speed increases?
questions.correctAnswerText: They increase.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and worse crashes. As speed increases, the impact force and risk of serious injury or death increase. Keep more distance between your vehicle and others when driving faster so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge. When parking uphill without a curb, turn them toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn them away from the curb.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke covering the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road, slow down immediately, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can hurt your eyes, lungs, or even be deadly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road entering from the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked cars are on your right. Where should you steer?
questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between them.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked cars are on your right, steer down the middle between both.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:
questions.correctAnswerText: Away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or when parking downhill, turn wheels toward the curb or road edge.
